title: Epochal Golden Harness with Graded Severity and Rollback Playback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current canary/eval pipeline uses static golden prompt sets and hard thresholds which frequently require manual tuning for different cohorts. This causes noisy rollouts and slow response when subtle quality regressions appear only for specific user cohorts or conversational contexts.

Goal: Implement an epochal golden-harness that: (1) maintains time-versioned golden prompt sets (epochs) to capture evolving user distributions, (2) scores canary/shadow traffic against epoch-aware scorecards, (3) maps score degradation into graded severity zones (green/yellow/orange/red) with progressive actions, and (4) enables a rollback-playback mode that replays traffic slices to help adjudicate noisy alerts prior to automated rollback.

Scope:
- Data model for epoched golden sets and metadata (source, coverage tags, sample weights).
- Scorecard computation engine supporting aggregated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE not suitable; use semantic similarity, response divergence, toxicity heuristics, and latency-sensitive heuristics).
- Severity zoning logic with hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.
- Rollout conductor integration: hook graded severity into the existing canary conductor so that: green=continue, yellow=notify+increased sampling, orange=quarantine traffic to shadow+notify SRE, red=initiate rollback-playback and possible auto-revert if confirmed.
- Rollback-playback: deterministic replay of the recent N minutes of canary traffic (with privacy-safe redaction) against the previous stable model and the candidate to provide side-by-side diff artifacts.
- UI surfaces in Console for epoch selector, severity timeline, sample diffs, and one-click rollback with audit trail.

Non-goals: Full automated adjudication of ambiguous failures (we will provide tools and graded automation but keep human-in-the-loop for orange/verdicts).

Success criteria:
- Reduce manual rollback incidents for subtle regressions by 40% in first 90 days.
- Provide replay artifacts for 95% of severity>=orange incidents.
- Integrate with existing rollout SLOs and not increase P50 latency for hosted traffic by more than 2ms due to gating checks.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached to Confluence link. Agreed on epoch naming convention: epoch_YYYYMM (rolling monthly) and a 'hot' epoch for emergent prompt ingestion.

2026-02-16 - Marco Nguyen: Initial schema drafted for epoch metadata (source, owner, coverage_tags, sampling_weight). Pushed PR to infra-models for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-models/pull/78

2026-02-20 - Elena Garcia (Design): Console mockups uploaded. Key request: allow customers to bind a rollout to a specific epoch or let it pick 'latest compatible' automatically. UX suggests showing per-epoch coverage heatmap.

2026-02-25 - Samir Rao (SRE): Raised concern about replay costs and burst capacity when doing rollback-playback. Proposed rate-limited playback and sampling heuristics (max 10k requests per playback, prefer stratified sampling by cohort).

2026-03-01 - Marco Nguyen: Implemented severity zoning engine prototype. Zones defined as: green (<1% regressions by weighted score), yellow (1-3%), orange (3-7%), red (>7%). These thresholds are configurable per-customer. Hysteresis window implemented: zone must persist for 3 evaluation intervals or meet sample quorum. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-engine/pull/206

2026-03-03 - QA: Ran synthetic divergence tests by injecting paraphrase noise into candidate model. Engine correctly flagged yellow->orange for targeted cohort; rollback-playback produced side-by-side diffs and a toxicity spike preview. Need to tighten replay redaction to remove PII in the sample payloads.

2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Requesting SRE sign-off on playback sampling limits and PM verification on customer-facing wording for severity states. Next steps: finish Console integration and end-to-end demo with solutions engineering next week.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints): schema + epoch ingestion service + scorecard prototype. Phase 2 (2 sprints): severity engine, hysteresis, and rollback-playback backend. Phase 3 (1 sprint): Console surfaces, e2e testing, and rollout conductor wiring. Phase 4: pilot with 2 customers and iterate thresholds.

Milestones: schema merged (2026-02-22), scorecard proto (2026-03-01), playback MVP (2026-03-12), Console beta (2026-03-18).
risks_mitigation: Risk: noisy thresholds causing false rollbacks. Mitigation: require hysteresis and sample quorum, and default to human-in-loop for orange events. Risk: privacy exposure during playback. Mitigation: automated redaction layer and opt-out toggles. Risk: production latency increase. Mitigation: async scoring with near-real-time windows and guardrails for request paths.
follow_up_tasks: Create infra ticket for redaction pipeline - ENG-574001
Pilot with BetaCorp and Atlas product teams
notes: This ticket forms the foundation for long-term eval-first rollouts. Consider extending epochs to support 'feature-tagged' golden sets for experiments tied to new prompt families.
